items.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I saw Leonard Bernstein just on the stage and hug Ornette down at the Five Spot.

ctx.x: I’m just learning stuff all the time. He said when it comes, when they lay those roses on you... Because you know if you start... the thing... the Bagavagida that I just recited to you. If you start pattin’ yourself on the back you’re gonna hit a tree man. It’s all in the mathematical basis of the universe. I think that’s what drew me to Bartok. I didn’t know what was going on, and he got that stuff from Fibonacci. And Fibonacci got it from the ancient African Egyptians or some people back there, you know. But…
You were getting to you don’t absorb these things.
